source_supported_pattern: The litigation concerned an ordinary termination during the KSchG waiting period.
The claimant was severely disabled; the employer knew the disability when hiring.
There was no works council and no representative body for severely disabled employees.
The employer asserted lack of professional suitability and stated that no other suitable vacancy existed.
The BAG held that a preventive procedure under section 167(1) SGB IX was not required during the KSchG waiting period and upheld the termination on the established facts.
synthetic_fixture_changes: The synthetic employee has more than six months tenure so the supplied Route B KSchG gates are exercisable.
The absence record, BEM process, health prognosis, operational impact, proportionality analysis, authority approval and AGG review are synthetic benchmark evidence.
The synthetic fixture is not evidence of what happened in the BAG litigation and must not be cited as a factual summary of that case.
